clock_dir_to: fraction-first "toward" direction ("un cuarto para las cuatro" == 3:45),
distinct from the hour-first "menos" subtraction ("las cuatro menos cuarto").
clock_meridiem_late: "tarde" is also the adverb "late": "A última hora, cuando el tiempo propicio
ya ha pasado [...]", e.g. "Has perdido el tren, llegaste tarde"
clock_meridiem_night: The NIGHT daypart is a BAND that crosses midnight in colloquial clock
usage, not a uniform +12 PM shift: "la una de la noche" is 01:00 and "las
doce de la noche" is midnight 00:00, while "las diez de la noche" is 22:00.
Small hours 1..5 stay AM, evening hours 6..11 are PM, twelve is midnight
(the band-split lives in the resolver _clock_hms).  The AM ceiling follows
the madrugada band [00:00, 06:00) transcribed for es in chronologia/
dayparts.py; colloquial "de la noche" for the small hours: RAE/DPD, s.v.
daypart_madrugada_es: Band boundaries: Unicode CLDR 47 Day Period Rules, locale es
Sources: Diccionario de la lengua espanola, RAE (https://dle.rae.es/tarde).
The small hours, which English has no single word for.
daypart_manana_es: Band boundaries: Unicode CLDR 47 Day Period Rules, locale es
Sources: Diccionario de la lengua espanola, RAE (https://dle.rae.es/tarde).
The bare word is NOT read here as the morning: "manana" is also the
Spanish for tomorrow, and that reading wins unless an article, a
demonstrative or "de" licenses the day-part one. See daypart_ref in
lang.json, which omits the bare order for exactly this reason.

marker_counted_noun: Nouns that count people or things a clock never takes: a bare hour behind a
clock preposition and directly before one of them is a count ("wave at 5
people").  Each word is quoted from its Wiktionary Noun entry
(https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/<word>); the fetched pages are kept with the audit.
marker_date_lead: Words that open a date or a clock time and belong to it.
Each word is shown opening a time or date phrase on the page named in brackets,
a: DLE "a" 6.: "Precisa el lugar o tiempo en que sucede algo. Firmaré a la noche." [rae-a.txt]
el: DLE "el" 2.: "unidades del calendario. ... El viernes empieza las vacaciones." [rae-el.txt]
marker_day_label: Spanish day-of-month label noun -- "día" ("day") heads the everyday idiom
"día N de <mes>" ("day 3 of March" == the 3rd of March), a genuine temporal
function word (RAE, Ortografía de la lengua española 5.2.5.1; DPD s.v.
"día") -- distinct from a bare ordinal reading, and NOT itself part of the
date construction's own grammar, so it was left stranded, unconsumed, in a
range endpoint's remainder even though the date it labels bound correctly.
Registered as its own marker so range-endpoint resolution
immediately-adjacent leading "día" into the consumed set precisely when the
date it labels actually bound -- never when the date fails to resolve, so a
"día" elsewhere in the sentence is untouched.
marker_dayframe: The frame Spanish puts in front of a part of the day ("por la mañana",
"por la tarde"). Unlike Galician "pola" and Portuguese "pela" the
preposition does not contract with the article, so the article follows it
Source: Diccionario de la lengua espanola, https://dle.rae.es/por.
marker_during: "en" is the locative preposition used with months ("en enero");
Source: Diccionario de la lengua espanola, https://dle.rae.es/en.
marker_from: Spanish range "from" lead -- opens a bounded or open interval and, crucially,
disambiguates the hyper-common preposition "a" (marker_to) as a genuine range
boundary: a bare "A a B" is only trusted as a range when a "from" lead is present.
"de": RAE/DPD s.v. "de" (preposicion) -- punto de partida / origen, correlativa
de "a" ("de junio a agosto"). Diccionario panhispanico de dudas (RAE-ASALE).
"desde": RAE, DLE s.v. "desde" (preposicion) -- punto de origen en el tiempo o
"a partir de": RAE -- locucion prepositiva, punto de comienzo.
"del": contraccion obligatoria de la preposicion "de" + el articulo "el"
(RAE-ASALE, Nueva gramatica de la lengua espanola, 21.3; Ortografia de la
lengua espanola, 3.4.2.2). Es la forma escrita corriente del inicio de un
intervalo cuando el termino lleva articulo: "del 5 al 12 de junio".
marker_half: period noun "mitad" (una de las dos partes iguales) -- RAE, Diccionario de la lengua española, s.v. "mitad".

correlativa de "de" ("de junio a agosto", "de 5 a 12").

kept alongside, as it is there.
